messages:
jamie: heads up — seeing steady memory creep from kv cache during long-context runs (~8k-12k tokens). reproducer attached to a local load test.

alex: interesting. is this paging or fragmentation?

jamie: profiler points at lots of tiny free fragments left behind by our small-block allocator after repeated kv writes/evicts. the total free bytes grow because holes don't coalesce. not normal paging churn.

sasha: can you paste the histogram?

jamie: ```
# alloc histogram (kv slab)
size_bucket,count
64,12842
128,4391
256,2301
512,112
1024,27
2048,3
>4096,0
total_allocated: 230MB
live_memory: 178MB
free_fragments: 23MB
largest_free_run: 512
```

maria: wow that 64/128 buckets are huge. small-chunk stickiness. does allocator have a per-shard freelist that prevents coalescing across pages?

jamie: yep — per-core freelists optimize latency but never merge across page boundaries. after long prefixes we end up with many isolated 64B and 128B holes.

tyler: did we try bumping the base block size? trading internal fragmentation for less external frag could help.

alex: agree. also consider a periodic background compact pass that scans hot slabs and merges adjacent free chunks into bigger slots. run low-priority to avoid p99 impacts.

jamie: tried simple pass in local dev: `compact_budget=100ms/s` where compact tries to merge contiguous free blocks up to 4k at a time. reduced free_fragments to 4MB but added +0.6ms p99 under heavy load.

sasha: 0.6ms p99 is not ideal. can we make compaction cooperative with request handling? e.g., piggyback a micro-compact when a thread is idle between requests.

maria: also think about adaptive block sizing: for long-context workloads, allocate a fraction of new pages with larger base granularity (e.g., 256B) so we don't create so many 64B fragments. config toggle per-route maybe.

jamie: good idea. my prototype added a `route_hint.long_context = true` flag and switched the shard's slab class target to 256B after 30s of long-seq traffic. memory steady-state improved w/o compaction.

tyler: can we detect long-context at runtime automatically? maybe track token runlength percentiles and flip classes when p95 > threshold.

alex: yes. heuristics: if avg_kv_size grows and eviction churn > X we flip. need safety: flip back on cold traffic.

kv-scrub-bot: scheduled a low-priority compact pass for node-7 at 03:10 UTC (budget=50ms).

sasha: curious about re-use behavior: when we promote older contexts/rollouts, do we excessively pin small fragments by keeping references?

jamie: good catch — we keep last-N context pointers to support quick reuse; that pins pages. reducing pinned history or moving pointers to a compacted index reduced pinning.

maria: TL;DR proposals to try in staging:
- adaptive slab-class switching per-route based on token runlengths
- cooperative micro-compaction piggybacked on idle cycles (budgeted)
- low-priority background compactor with strict time budget and backoff when p99 rises
- audit pinned-context retention policy (reduce N or use compressed index)

jamie: I'll open a PR with the adaptive class switch prototype and the micro-compact hook. posting perf numbers soon.

alex: please include a microbenchmark for churned allocations (simulate open/close of many small keys) and the long-context load. want before/after p95/p99 and mem graphs.

jamie: will do. quick note: traces show fragmentation plateauing after ~20 minutes with current heuristics but still ~12MB wasted on >10k contexts. hope to get that to <2MB.

sasha: sounds good. ping me on the PR for review — will check contended locks and per-core freelist interactions.

tyler: if we need a fast rollback, make the adaptive switch opt-in via config flag.

jamie: yep — plan: feature-flag, tests, perf-run on staging, then gradual rollout. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: awesome. one more: add metric `kv.frag_ratio_by_bucket` so we can monitor which bucket sizes cause the most waste in prod.

jamie: added to the TODO in the PR.

kv-scrub-bot: compaction pass completed on node-7 (used 42ms, freed 3.6MB).
